title: Exact symbol sequence for morphisms into an injectively graded filtered object
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with Hom groups taken in a common larger universe. Let $(X,F)$ and $(Y,F)$ be objects with finite decreasing filtrations by subobjects [def-sp-filtration]: there are integers $a\le b$ and $c\le d$ with $F^aX=X$, $F^{b+1}X=0$, $F^cY=Y$, and $F^{d+1}Y=0$. Suppose that each $\operatorname{gr}^qY=F^qY/F^{q+1}Y$ is injective in the extension-property sense [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For $r\in\mathbf Z$ define the subgroup
$$G^r(X,Y)=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,Y)\mid f(F^pX)\subseteq F^{p+r}Y\text{ for all }p\in\mathbf Z\}.$$
For $f\in G^r(X,Y)$ let $\sigma_r(f)_p:\operatorname{gr}^pX\to\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}Y$ be the map induced by $f|_{F^pX}$. Then the sequence of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow G^{r+1}(X,Y)\longrightarrow G^r(X,Y)\xrightarrow{\sigma_r}\bigoplus_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\operatorname{gr}^pX,\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}Y)\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. The direct sum is finite because $\operatorname{gr}^pX=0$ outside $[a,b]$. The induced isomorphism from $G^r/G^{r+1}$ to this sum is natural under precomposition by filtration-preserving maps $X'\to X$ between finite filtered objects, and under postcomposition by filtration-preserving maps $Y\to Y'$ between finite filtered objects whose graded pieces are injective.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective. Agent-extracted symbol-sequence consequence of its split-filtration description and the injective extension property of def-sp-injective-resolutions; the exact symbol sequence is not printed verbatim in Tag 05TP.

proof.text: Choose the bounds c,d for Y from the finite-filtration hypotheses. Apply [lem-trf-injective-graded-filtration-splits] to obtain injective objects J_q and an isomorphism θ:Y ≅ ⊕_{c≤q≤d}J_q identifying F^tY with the tail ⊕_{q≥t}J_q. For each p, the inclusion F^pX→X followed by X→X/F^{p+1}X identifies gr^pX with a subobject of X/F^{p+1}X (the kernel is exactly F^{p+1}X by the induced and quotient filtration definitions). Given a finite family of graded maps α_p:gr^pX→gr^{p+r}Y, compose α_p with the isomorphism gr^{p+r}Y ≅ θ(F^{p+r}Y)/θ(F^{p+r+1}Y) = ⊕_{q≥p+r}J_q/⊕_{q≥p+r+1}J_q ≅ J_{p+r} induced by θ (the J_{p+r}-coordinate of the tail; when p+r lies outside [c,d] both sides are 0, take J_{p+r}=0 and α_p=0); injectivity of J_{p+r} extends it along this monomorphism to δ_p:X/F^{p+1}X→J_{p+r}.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; split filtration and componentwise extension property

proof.text: Compose each δ_p with X→X/F^{p+1}X, include its value in the J_{p+r} summand, transport back by θ^{-1}, and sum over the finitely many p with gr^pX≠0. Call the resulting map f:X→Y. If x lies in F^kX, the summands with p<k vanish because F^kX⊆F^{p+1}X, while the summands with p≥k land in J_{p+r}⊆F^{k+r}Y; hence f∈G^r(X,Y). On the pth graded quotient (composite F^pX→F^{p+r}Y→gr^{p+r}Y), the summands with p'>p land in F^{p+r+1}Y and vanish, and the pth summand is α_p because the θ-induced isomorphism gr^{p+r}Y≅J_{p+r} of step 1 is the J_{p+r}-projection of the tail, so σ_r(f)=(α_p)_p. This proves surjectivity of σ_r; finiteness of the sum follows from the finite interval for X.

source.place: Tag 05TP, finite direct-sum construction and filtration-tail calculation

proof.text: If f∈G^r has σ_r(f)=0, then for every p the composite F^pX→F^{p+r}Y→gr^{p+r}Y is zero. Since F^{p+r+1}Y is the kernel of the quotient map defining gr^{p+r}Y, the image f(F^pX) is contained in F^{p+r+1}Y. Thus f∈G^{r+1}. Conversely G^{r+1}⊆G^r and every such map has zero symbol by definition, so ker(σ_r)=G^{r+1}. The first map is the inclusion and is injective, proving exactness at the first two terms.

source.place: Tag 05TP, quotient-kernel characterization of the graded component

proof.text: For a filtration-preserving map X'→X, restriction and passage to the quotient commute with precomposition, so each symbol component of f∘u is the corresponding component of σ_r(f)∘gr(u). For a filtration-preserving map v:Y→Y', the inclusions v(F^qY)⊆F^qY' induce maps gr^qY→gr^qY', and the same restriction/quotient calculation gives σ_r(v∘f)=gr(v)∘σ_r(f). These identities respect the inclusions G^{r+1}⊆G^r and the finite direct sums. If Y' has injective graded pieces, the preceding exactness applies to Y' as well, so the induced quotient isomorphisms are natural under both kinds of maps.

lean.statement: theorem injectiveTargetHomSymbol (X Y : FilteredObject C) (a b c d : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b) (hcd : c ≤ d) (hXa : X.filtration.F a = ⊤) (hXb : X.filtration.F (b + 1) = ⊥) (hYc : Y.filtration.F c = ⊤) (hYd : Y.filtration.F (d + 1) = ⊥) (hgr : ∀ q : ℤ, Injective (Y.filtration.gr q)) (r : ℤ) : filteredHomSubgroup X Y (r + 1) ≤ filteredHomSubgroup X Y r ∧ (∀ f : filteredHomSubgroup X Y r, filteredHomSymbol X Y r a b f = 0 ↔ f.1 ∈ filteredHomSubgroup X Y (r + 1)) ∧ Function.Surjective (filteredHomSymbol X Y r a b) ∧ (∀ (X' : FilteredObject C) (a' b' : ℤ), a' ≤ b' → X'.filtration.F a' = ⊤ → X'.filtration.F (b' + 1) = ⊥ → ∀ (u : FilteredObject.Hom X' X) (f : filteredHomSubgroup X Y r) (p : ℤ), shiftedGradedMapHom X' Y r p (precompHom X' X Y r u f) = FilteredObject.gradedMap u p ≫ shiftedGradedMapHom X Y r p f) ∧ (∀ (Y' : FilteredObject C) (c' d' : ℤ), c' ≤ d' → Y'.filtration.F c' = ⊤ → Y'.filtration.F (d' + 1) = ⊥ → (∀ q : ℤ, Injective (Y'.filtration.gr q)) → ∀ (v : FilteredObject.Hom Y Y') (f : filteredHomSubgroup X Y r) (p : ℤ), shiftedGradedMapHom X Y' r p (postcompHom X Y Y' r v f) = shiftedGradedMapHom X Y r p f ≫ FilteredObject.gradedMap v (p + r))
